text:
Sam L: Canary report: Dedicated pool running Mistral-7b-v0.2+fp8-kvcache shows +12% memory vs baseline and a couple of soft OOMs during long prefixes. rolling it back for now :eyes:
Anya R: saw the alert. is this from the fp8 packing change we merged yesterday?
Kevin M: yep, PR #421 changed the KV pack layout to channel-major for fp8 to improve vectorized stores. intended mem win, not loss.
Sam L: attaching quick profile snippet from the failing instance:
```
PID  12345  rss=43.1G  kvcache_mem=13.4G  tensor_mem=26.3G
kvcache_format=fp8_packed_channel_major  entries=4.9M  avg_entry_bytes=2760
batching_groups=8  avg_seq=1536  padded_seq=2048
```
Anya R: padded_seq=2048 is huge — looks like batching heuristic pushed max pad for these requests. that blows up kv cache since we store prefix per head*seq.
Julie P: might be two orthogonal problems: packing density + padding multiplier. packing changed layout so our per-entry rounding/pad logic produces slightly larger stride.
Kevin M: confirmed: channel-major introduced a 64-byte tail per head-block due to our 32->8-bit packing width alignment. for Mistral heads=64 kv_dim=1280 that tail multiplies.
Sam L: also observed regressions in kernel selection: fp16 kernels were picked for some kernels but fallbacks to generic kernel happened when kv format was fp8, leading to more temporary buffers. logs show: `selected_kernel=matmul_fp16_v2 fallback=matmul_generic`
ml-bot: perf/regression detected: kvcache_bytes +11.8% and peak_allocations +9.5% during step 600-800 of perf run.
Infra-bot: alert auto-mitigations: scaled pool up by +1 node and restarted canary.
Anya R: hypothesis: when kv cache is packed fp8 channel-major, our kernel scheduler can't use specialized matmul_fp8 kernels (they expect head-major layout). scheduler then inserts reorder + unpack which increases mem.
Kevin M: reproducer command I used:
```
python -m perf.run --model=mistral-7b-v0.2 --seq=2048 --batch=4 \
  --kv-precision=fp8 --kv-pack=channel-major --requests=1000
```
Kevin M: profiler flame snippet shows large time in `reorder_unpack_kernel` and extra allocation spikes during first token of each batch group.
Julie P: Qwen/Mixtral configs might behave differently since they have different head and kv dims. we should triage by model to verify which combos hit ordering mismatch.
Sam L: quick matrix to run: Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen-7B with kv_precision=[fp16, bf16, fp8], kv_pack=[head-major, channel-major], seq=[512, 1536, 2048]. we should log `selected_kernel` per op.
Anya R: I also noticed prefix-cache interactions: when prefix-caching is enabled we dedupe prefix tensors across requests, but our dedupe key ignores pack-layout. so channel-major and head-major variants end up as separate cache entries -> duplication.
Kevin M: brutal: that means switch to fp8 packed channel-major caused duplication of cached prefixes (roughly x2) when we had a mixed pool during rollout. explains memory jump.
Sam L: immediate mitigation: 1) roll back kv-pack default to head-major 2) make dedupe key include (kv_precision, kv_pack) 3) make scheduler prefer matmul_fp8-compatible kernels when kv_pack==head-major
Julie P: long-term: upstream kernels should accept both layouts or we add tiny zero-copy remap kernels. also consider per-model pack strategy: e.g., mixtral prefers head-major to match its kernels, whereas Qwen prefers channel-major for memory throughput.
Anya R: small experiment idea: quantized int8 for KV entries (per-channel scale) could cut memory, but we need to evaluate round-trip noise for Llama-style scaling. Also eviction policy: current LRU evicts by entries, but with large padded_seq the effective memory gain is negligible. propose segment-aware eviction (evict oldest prefix segments first).
Kevin M: added a quick patch to repo on a branch: `kvcache/dedupe-key-fix` — makes key include precision+pack and adds a metric `kvcache_duplicate_keys` for monitoring.
Sam L: can we get a canary with kvcache dedupe fix + forced kv_pack=head-major for Mistral only? test matrix: keep others rolling.
Infra-bot: canary scheduled: pool=d-ed-3, image=canary-kvfix-2026-03-17, start=1778452200
ml-bot: suggestion: add eval prompts with long prefixes (>1500) and mixed-history to exercise eviction and dedupe. we have a suite: `eval/prefix_regression.long_prefix.jsonl`
Julie P: one more observation: RoPE scaling interacts — when we scale RoPE (scale >1) we change position-dependent kv sparsity pattern, which for some packing layouts induces less compressibility and slightly larger packed size. not huge but contributes.
Anya R: action items:
- Kevin: run model matrix and record selected_kernel + kvcache_bytes per run (due 1778454000)
- Kevin: push canary with dedupe fix + head-major for mistral (in flight)
- Julie: draft kernel compatibility doc listing which kernels expect which pack layouts (due EOD)
- Infra: watch kvcache_duplicate_keys metric and OOM alerts for canary
Sam L: thanks. keep updates short here. if we get green with dedupe fix we can reintroduce channel-major with explicit kernel changes later. :thumbsup:
Anya R: noted. I'll also add a test that ensures prefix cache dedupe key includes layout to prevent future regressions.
Kevin M: starting matrix run now. ping when infra canary is up.
Sam L: 👍
